output.reason: A small, itchy, non-spreading forearm rash beginning after gardening fits an irritant or allergic contact reaction and can be managed with self-care guidance plus clear escalation triggers.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now: wash the area and any gardening clothes, avoid re-contact, and use a gentle moisturizer; an OTC hydrocortisone cream or oral antihistamine may ease itching. Seek same-day care if the rash becomes painful, warm, swollen or spreads, if blisters or oozing appear, or if you develop fever. Call 911 for any throat tightness, trouble breathing, or facial swelling.
differential: Contact dermatitis from a plant or garden irritant
